title: Orchard deploy weekly check inventory and notes (May 2028)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working weekly deployment binder for the Orchard feature rollout (May 6–12, 2028). Focus: incremental canary expansion, paired smoke suites, and a short post-release retro checklist. This doc is intentionally conversational — use as operator desk notes during the week.

Context and scope:
- Orchard is a routing shim that enables model variant pinning + burst autoscale. Non-user-facing config; affects serving paths for Hosted API.
- Release window targeted: Tue May 7 10:00–14:00 PT (quiet window).
- Risk profile: medium (changes touching routing + cache warming).

Week-of calendar (high level):
- Mon May 6: Dry-run + preflight rehearsals (09:00–12:00). Verify canary infra, capacity.
- Tue May 7: Day-of deploy. 10:00 start; stepwise traffic ramp (see rollout ladder).
- Wed May 8: Nightwatch (24h after first traffic shift) — telemetry sampling and regression checks.
- Thu May 9: Full traffic sweep if green; start softbackfilling of prefetched caches.
- Fri May 10: Postmortem notes collection + initial retro.

Preflight checklist (must be green before 10:00 Tue):
- [ ] CI green on master and release branch; no blocked PRs (PR #187).
- [ ] Canary fleet reserved: 8x g5-like nodes in us-west-2 (capacity verified).
- [ ] Canary autoscale policy staged and dry-run results attached to REL-2205.
- [ ] Smoke suites updated: orch-smoke v2 includes KV lookup and prefix-cache asserts.
- [ ] Dashboard snapshots created (token-cost, p95 latency, error-rate) for baseline.
- [ ] Slack bridge created: #orchard-deploy and escalation to @oncall-sre.
- [ ] Oncall + shift leads confirmed: Marcus (day), Sofia (night).

Rollout ladder (minute-by-minute highlights):
- T+0 (10:00): flip feature-flag orchard.enabled -> canary cohort 0.5% traffic. TTL: 15m.
- T+15: smoke run (orch-smoke v2) against canary cohort. Quick checks: 200 OK rate, kv-hits >= 98%, p95 < baseline*1.2.
- T+30: expand to 2% if smoke green. Monitor error-rate < 0.5% absolute increase.
- T+60: expand to 10% if stable for 30m with no regressions.
- T+120: 50% expansion gated on cost-SLO and sample-quality checks.
- T+240: 100% if all gates pass and oncall signoff.

Telemetry gating thresholds (explicit):
- Error rate: no more than +0.5 percentage points vs baseline over 30m window.
- Latency (p95): < baseline + 120ms for Hosted API common routes.
- Token inflation / cost: per-token median increase < 10% vs baseline.
- Quality regression: run sampling eval (eval set orchard-weekly-2028-05); zero critical label flips in sample of 500.
- If ANY gate fails, immediate rollback to previous routing snapshot and open incident channel.

Smoke and validation runbook (what to run):
- orch-smoke v2 (automated): kv read/write, cache warm, route validation, model variant check.
- perf-sample: 1k synthetic requests across 5 locales (us, eu, apac).
- human-check: 10 live queries (SEs + product) verifying conversational outputs for hallucination / truncation.

Rollback decision matrix (quick):
- Trigger: absolute error-rate spike > 1.5% or sustained >0.8% for 30m => Action: rollback to routing snapshot -1, notify customers if impacted.
- Trigger: p95 > baseline + 250ms for 15m => Action: pause expansion, run targeted investigations (kernel/quantization), alert infra.
- Trigger: critical eval flips (>5/500) => Action: immediate rollback + revert PR.

Operator comms & run-of-show (short):
- Preflight ping (30m before start): #orchard-deploy channel post baseline + checklist tick.
- At each ladder step: post status summary (cohort, p95, err, sample-check) to channel.
- If rolling forward to 100%: confirm with Marcus and Sofia in channel and tag @product-ops.

Post-release (first 48h):
- Telemetry sampling: increase logging for routing decisions by 10% (sample rate).
- Retrospective collection: collect noisy traces, customer-facing errors, and a 10-line summary for execs.
- Cost check: compare token units per hour vs baseline and flag >12% deviation.

Operator notes & friction points (notes to self):
- Cache warm-up sometimes lags behind routing expansion — consider increasing pre-warm traffic to canary hosts by synthetic-burst pre-step.
- Locales: apac latency spike last dry-run — possible regional kernel selection mismatch. Need follow-up with infra.
- TODO: add an explicit KV cache TTL extension step to preflight (ticket REL-2208).

Quick links and artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchard/pull/187
- Linear: https://linear.app/RD/issue/RI-4823-deploy-orchard-weekly
- Telemetry dashboards: (link to dashboard saved in REL-2205)

Retro prompts (to fill out after Fri):
- What surprised us?
- Where did automation fail or help?
- Did sampling catch edge regressions?
- Actionables: assign owners and due dates.

Unresolved questions (for the postmortem):
- Is the cache pre-warming approach sustainable under bursts?
- Do we need a permanent 0.1% observability cohort for ongoing drift detection?
- Should model-variant pins be exposed to platform teams as a toggle?

If anything goes wrong: escalate to @oncall-sre and follow the Incident Ops playbook (link: Confluence REL-INCIDENTS).

-- Aisha (notes)
